title: Your inner teacher
tomorrow: fix yourself first, or go help now?

cards: When a founder steps down, everyone wants to know who's next: the band, the startup, the family business.
Near the end, the Buddha was old and had been gravely ill, and Ananda took comfort in one thought: surely he'll leave instructions about the sangha before he goes. The reply is strange on purpose.
He says he has taught without a closed fist, holding nothing back as a secret, and he has never thought of himself as the one the sangha depends on. Then he names who teaches now.

teach.b: In Rhys Davids' old translation: "Be ye lamps unto yourselves." Be a refuge to yourselves, he goes on, with the teaching as your lamp and refuge, and no other. Here's the puzzle.
How can you be your own refuge and also take refuge in the teaching? Two clues sit in the text. First, the word.

teach.h: DIPA: A LAMP, OR AN ISLAND.
teach.b: The Pali dipa can be read as lamp or as island, and translators split; either way, it's something to see by or stand on when the water rises. Second, the Buddha says how.
A monk is his own lamp when he practices mindfulness of the body, of feelings, of the mind, and of the teachings themselves. So the inner teacher isn't a hunch or a mood.
It's attention, trained by the teaching until it can see for itself. That's the same thread as the Kalamas, told to know for themselves, and the monks told to check even him.
On Thursday, Mai asked the visiting teacher whether it's okay that she doesn't chant along. He didn't answer. He asked: when you sit through the chanting, what do you notice?

how: Buddhist teachers often answer a student's question with a question, pointing them back to their own practice; the Buddha's words 'be lamps (or islands) unto yourselves' are often quoted as a reminder that the teaching is tested in one's own mindfulness.

o: attention, trained by the teaching, that can see for itself
the first teacher you ever had, remembered with thanks
a guardian spirit that whispers advice to meditators

games.q: the last advice — tap the pairs.
p: hoped for instructions about the sangha
nothing held back as a secret
how to be your own lamp

s: the Buddha named a successor to lead the sangha after him
he pointed to the teaching, and each person's own practice, as lamp and refuge.
the Pali word in this passage can be read as lamp or as island
translators split; Rhys Davids chose lamps.
'be your own lamp' means trust whatever you happen to feel
the text says how: mindfulness of body, feelings, mind and the teachings.

games.q: a friend says her inner teacher told her to quit everything and move away tomorrow, no talking it over. what fits the Buddha's last advice?
o: sit with the feeling, see it clearly, and test it by the teaching first
trust it: the Buddha said you are your own refuge, full stop
ignore it: inner voices are just ego, so follow a teacher instead
games.why: the lamp is attention trained by the teaching, not a sudden mood. the Buddha joined 'be your own refuge' to 'the teaching as your refuge' in one breath.

practice: Close your eyes if that's comfortable, and sit with whatever is here: the body's weight, a feeling, the mood of the mind. Don't fix any of it; just see it clearly.
If one honest insight comes, small or plain, let it stay without arguing.

wordCard.voice: Your inner teacher: attention trained by the teaching until it can see for itself, a lamp you carry.

orig.note: Pali: a lamp, or an island; the word in 'be a lamp unto yourselves'.

carryVoice: Your line: know for yourself, by the light the teaching gives you. Twenty days of the block, lit.

sources.tr: Rhys Davids 1881 (Sacred Books of the East XI)
